merged.title: Optimise Vulkan water and draw uploads
merged.author: pezzadev
merged.untrustedBody:
## Summary

- Cache baked water strip meshes across visibility changes and draw each strip once.
- Use indexed Vulkan effect quads and upload only dirty joint-palette rows when changes are sparse.
- Declare Vulkan GPU culling dependencies in the render graph and add opt-in Tracy timings for presentation and temporal work.

- Windows Vulkan viewer, effects pixel-equivalence, FSR motion, water mesh, and presentation tests passed, including swapchain synchronization validation.

- PAL and NTSC retail gameplay and other platforms were not rerun for this draft.

merged.title: fix(port): preserve register banks in level-copy calls
merged.author: llesieur99
merged.untrustedBody:
## Problem

The Insomniac Museum can crash while drawing a shared sign-band effect on Windows x64. The shared callback resolves the correct level-specific helper, but invokes it through the canonical helper's mixed nine-argument prototype. The Museum helper takes six integer arguments, so its object pointer is read from the stack slot containing a random float. Its first `object + 0x68` access then reads an unmapped guest address.

## Change

Route mixed-argument `call_copies` calls through the existing register-bank dispatcher and the selected callee's registered thunk. Each callee receives integers and floats in the order the EE passes them. This also preserves the executable-versus-level target choice and wide result types.

Add generator regressions for both target-selection paths and an offline runtime regression exercising the canonical mixed signature and the Museum-style six-integer signature.

## Validation

- The new generator regression fails in both subcases before the fix

merged.title: fix(vulkan): stop Mali GPUs crashing at the title screen
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
**Before:** on Android with a Mali GPU (Mali-G57, driver r54p1) the game crashed at the title screen with Vulkan, now the default. The crash was in the driver's shader compiler while it made the world's first pipeline. Arm's Mali Offline Compiler segfaults the same way on any vertex shader that writes `gl_ClipDistance`, on every Mali core from G52 to G720. mesh.vert, mesh_depth.vert and shadow_depth.vert all write it.

**After:** on Arm devices, and on any device without `shaderClipDistance`, vkgl sends the vertex stages' clip distances to a plain variable, as the ES path already does without `GL_EXT_clip_cull_distance`. The only loss is the cut of the 2D layer's mobys at the picture's sides on a wide target, as on ES. Other GPUs get the same shaders as before. Until Vulkan is played on a Mali device, the Android launcher starts the game with OpenGL ES on Mali unless the player picked a renderer. Picking Vulkan is now saved as a choice.

**How:** `vertex_clip_distance` in `shader_compi

merged.title: fix(vulkan): keep the world in one render pass under the render graph
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
Since the render graph (#225) every world layer began a render pass of its own: declaring a pass's inputs ended the open pass, and so did entering a pass whose only barriers were attachment writes after attachment writes. On Orxon with 4x MSAA a frame had 17 passes instead of 3 and loaded and stored 147/155 MB of attachments instead of 20/25 MB. A tiled phone GPU pays that in memory traffic: a Galaxy S26 Ultra fell from 120 fps to 40-90 the longer it played.

The open pass now ends only for its own attachments: a sampled texture's or another image's import leaves it open, an attachment the pass has already drawn into is imported as written, and a graph pass whose barriers are all attachment-to-attachment in the same layout draws on in it (draws in one pass keep their order). Orxon, 4x MSAA: 3 passes, 15/22 MB, the frame pixel for pixel the same.

merged.title: fix(launcher): never offer a Rebuild that cannot make a missing game program
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
A player on a Steam Deck reported that Going Commando keeps asking to be built. Every build reads the levels from the disc, the export ends normally, and then the launcher asks again.

## Cause

Launcher 1.0.0's installer carries no Going Commando program. CI builds only `rac1-pal` and `rac1-ntsc`, and v0.10.0 didn't build it either. The installer also carries no `port-build` for rac2, because `KEEP` dropped it. 1.0.0 opened rac2's Play to players, but Play still needs `port/build/release/openrac-rac2-ntsc.exe`.

With no build action, `rebuildSteps` falls back to the Android path and reads the levels again (`port-levels`). That run succeeds and writes `levels-20.json`. Play is still blocked on the missing program, so `playerState` offers "Rebuild" again, and the loop never ends.

opened.untrustedBody:
